 Scotty Pippen Jr. (back) is out for Monday’s game against the Pelicans. 
 Pippen will miss a second straight game after sitting out Saturday’s win over the Kings. His absence won’t significantly impact fantasy basketball, as Ty Jerome (back) is available. Javon Small could play a few minutes off the bench, but that isn’t guaranteed. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Scotty Pippen Jr. (back) is doubtful for Monday’s game against the Pelicans. 
 Pippen did not play in Saturday’s win over the Kings and appears likely to remain out on Monday. Ty Jerome (back) is available, so Pippen remaining out would not put the Grizzlies in a terrible spot. Javon Small could play some off the bench after logging 20 minutes on Saturday, but that isn’t guaranteed. 
 Scotty Pippen 
 MEM 
 Guard 
 #1 
 Scotty Pippen Jr. (back) is out for Saturday’s game against the Kings. 
 The Grizzlies will be without two rotation guards on Saturday, as Pippen and Ty Jerome (back) are out. Cam Spencer will play more minutes and is worth streaming in deep leagues. 
 Ty Jerome 
 MEM 
 Guard-Forward 
 #2 
 Ty Jerome (upper back) and Scotty Pippen Jr. (lower back) are questionable to play against the Kings on Saturday. 
 Ty Jerome has been one of the biggest surprises this season and has been a major steal for where people drafted him in redraft leagues. If he were to miss time, Scotty Pippen would be the guy to add in redraft leagues. If Pippen also misses time, then look at Cam Spencer to be the add. 
 Ty Jerome 
 MEM 
 Guard-Forward 
 #2 
 Ty Jerome struggled on Thursday and finished with just 10 points (3-of-12 FGs), two rebounds, three assists, two steals and one three-pointer against the Trail Blazers. 
 Less than an hour before tipoff, it was reported that Jerome was questionable for this game with back tightness. Despite the flare up, he was able to start, though it ended up being his worst performance of the season, and he only played 24 minutes. This is worth keeping an eye on, especially ahead of their next game against the Kings on Saturday. Cam Spencer and Scotty Pippen Jr. would fill out the point guard minutes if Jerome were unavailable. 
 Cedric Coward 
 MEM 
 Guard 
 #23 
 Cedric Coward (wrist) is doubtful for Friday’s game against the Warriors. 
 Coward, who played 28 minutes in Wednesday’s win over the Jazz, is dealing with a sprained left wrist. With the doubtful tag, he’s more likely to miss Friday. If Coward sits, reserves like Scotty Pippen Jr. and Jerami Grant would get more offensive opportunities. 
 Ty Jerome 
 MEM 
 Guard-Forward 
 #2 
 Ty Jerome accumulated 12 points (4-of-8 FGs, 3-of-3 FTs), five assists and one block over 15 minutes in Monday’s preseason win over the Hawks. 
 It’s notable that Jerome got the start over Scotty Pippen Jr. during Memphis’ preseason opener and he responded by pouring in 10 first-half points on 4-of-8 shooting as Memphis exploded for 82 points in an impressive opening half. It’s fair to wonder whether Jerome can build off his initial success with the Grizzlies last year when he averaged 19.7 points while shooting over 42 percent from three-point range after finally making his season debut in late January. 
 Scotty Pippen 
 MEM 
 Guard 
 #1 
 Scotty Pippen Jr. (toe) will undergo season-ending surgery on his right great toe. 
 Having missed the Grizzlies’ last three games with sesamoiditis in his right great toe, Pippen will now undergo a season-ending sesamoidectomy to address the issue. He underwent a similar procedure in October, which delayed the guard’s season debut until early February. Pippen only appeared in ten games this season, finishing with averages of 11.4 points, 2.2 rebounds, 4.7 assists, 1.9 steals and 1.0 three-pointers in 21.2 minutes. With Ty Jerome having recently missed some games, Javon Small and Cam Spencer will have added fantasy value for the rest of this season.

 Scotty Pippen Jr. (toe) is out for Thursday’s game against the Mavericks. 
 Pippen will miss a third consecutive game as he continues to deal with sesamoiditis in his right great toe. Javon Small and, if available, Cam Spencer will play plenty, as the Grizzlies are unlikely to have Ty Jerome (calf) as well. 
 Santi Aldama 
 MEM 
 Forward-Center 
 #7 
 Santi Aldama (knee) and Scotty Pippen Jr. (toe) are out for Tuesday’s matchup with the 76ers. 
 Memphis’ injury report is lengthy, and with Aldama out again, Olivier-Maxence Prosper should continue to start and see meaningful minutes. Pippen Jr.'s continued absence means more run for Ty Jerome and Cam Spencer.

 #1 
 Scotty Pippen Jr. (toe) is out for Monday’s game against the Nets. 
 Initially doubtful for Monday’s game, Pippen is now officially out. Cam Spencer, Walter Clayton Jr. and Javon Small take on added importance within the Grizzlies’ rotation, as Ty Jerome is also out.

 Derik Queen provided a boost off the bench with 20 points (7-of-13 FGs), seven rebounds, five assists, two steals, one block and one three-pointer against the Grizzlies on Monday.
 Queen was fantastic off the bench in this game, especially early on. He scored 18 points in 15 minutes in the first half alone, and while he cooled off after that, it still ended up being a productive outing for him. Queen has been productive this season despite a disappointing lack of minutes, and he made the most of his time on the floor in this one. However, his ceiling will continue to be capped as a reserve despite his fantasy-friendly game.
 -  Noah Rubin

 Karlo Matković lit up the Grizzlies with 25 points (9-of-13 FGs), six rebounds, one assist, two steals, one block and five three-pointers on Monday.
 Matković has started the last three games for New Orleans, and while he has been productive, this was by far his best performance. He set career highs for both points and three-pointers, and New Orleans needed every single one of them to get the win. Matković has averaged 15.0 points, 6.7 rebounds, 2.0 steals, 1.0 block and 2.7 triples as a starter and is still available in 94 percent of Yahoo! leagues.
 -  Noah Rubin

 Tyrese Maxey led the 76ers with 26 points (10-of-15 FGs), four rebounds, 11 assists, two steals, two blocks and one three-pointer in a 126-107 win over the Bulls on Monday.
 On this revamped 76ers team, Maxey hasn’t done as much playmaking as he has in recent years. However, he played the facilitator role well in this game, shattering his previous season high for assists of six on his way to his first double-double of the season. Maxey has been a superstar once again this season, and while his dimes have been down, his scoring and field goal percentage have both been up. The dimes likely won’t continue to this level, but he can still chip in from time to time.
 -  Noah Rubin

 Jaylen Brown recorded a double-double on Monday with 25 points (9-of-15 FGs), 11 rebounds, five assists, one steal and four three-pointers against the Bulls.
 Brown had a quieter performance on Saturday, which was his return from a one-game absence with a knee injury. He was able to get back on track in this one with he second 20-point double-double in his last three appearances. Brown’s opportunities may have dropped this year, but when he has his shot going like he did in this one, he’s still capable of making a massive impact. He’ll look to keep it up in Detroit on Wednesday.

 Tyler Herro had 21 points (8-of-18 FGs, 1-of-2 FTs), six rebounds, three assists, three steals and four three-pointers against the Timberwolves on Monday. 
 Herro was hardly efficient on Monday with 21 points on 18 attempts. He made four three-pointers and added three steals on the defensive end. Herro has scored at least 21 points in five of seven games with the Bucks to start the season. Milwaukee will travel to Boston for a road matchup against the Celtics Wednesday.

 VJ Edgecombe lit up the Bulls with 21 points (9-of-12 FGs), three rebounds, five assists, one steal, one block and two three-pointers on Monday.
 Edgecombe started this game off strong, entering halftime with 15 points on a perfect 7-of-7 shooting. He cooled off after the break, but he was still able to post a full stat line and set a new season high for scoring. Edgecombe has still been productive in fantasy basketball this season, though his scoring has predictably dropped off. However, he’s still more than capable of having hot shooting nights like this one.

 Daniel Gafford accumulated 20 points (9-of-10 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), seven rebounds, one steal and one block in Monday’s loss to the Kings.
 The Kings struggled to find an answer for Gafford in the second quarter, when he tied his career-high for points in a quarter with 11. He didn’t produce much in the second half, but many fantasy managers will take that final stat line from DG. With Dereck Lively II and Santi Aldama still sidelined, Gafford has played nearly 24 minutes per game. And so far, his production has exceeded his preseason ADP by a safe distance. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Walter Clayton Jr. produced 20 points (6-of-9 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), one rebound, two assists, one steal and four three-pointers in Monday’s loss to the Kings.
 No Kyrie Irving (knee) led to Clayton playing rotation minutes on Monday, and he took advantage of the opportunity. Shooting 3-of-4 from the field, the second-year guard scored nine points in the first half. After Max Christie was ruled out with a hip injury, Clayton entered the lineup to start the third quarter. Whether he has value for Wednesday’s game against the Spurs will depend on Irving’s and Christie’s availability. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Ayo Dosunmu had 19 points (8-of-18 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), 12 rebounds, eight assists, one steal, one block and one three-pointer against the Bucks on Monday. 
 While LaMelo Ball erupted for 34 points in this one, Dosunmu may be the real fantasy winner from Anthony Edwards (knee) having to miss time with an injury. Dosunmu had a full stat line and was two assists shy of a triple-double in the win over the Bucks. He should be rostered in all formats at this point. 
 -  Nick Shlain

 Cooper Flagg accounted for 17 points (3-of-19 FGs, 11-of-11 FTs), four rebounds, six assists and two steals in Monday’s loss to the Kings.
 Without Kyrie Irving (knee), the Mavericks had to rely even more on Flagg offensively. Unfortunately, the reigning Rookie of the Year couldn’t buy a bucket, shooting 3-of-15 from two and missing all four of his three-point attempts. Flagg’s ability to get to the foul line boosted the point total, and the assist production was solid. However, between the poor shooting and the six turnovers, this was a bad night for him.
